Let me work through this as the CFO persona. The persona priorities: credible traceable business case, total cost of ownership over contract life, cash flow timing and funding source, auditability and control environment, flexibility to scale or exit.

Criteria:
- C1: Annualized TCO (cost) — directly maps to CFO priority #2.
- C2: Expected annual productivity benefit — maps to business case credibility (#1).
- C3: Integration effort (person-days) — cost of implementation, cash flow timing, change bandwidth.
- C4: Expected annual data-exposure and compliance loss — auditability and control environment (#4).
- C5: Sustained throughput at latency ceiling — technical performance; less directly a CFO concern, but relates to whether benefit materializes.
- C6: Onboarding time to proficiency — user cost, change-management bandwidth, affects realization of benefits.

As CFO: C1 (TCO) is top. C4 (compliance loss) matters due to auditability/control and regulatory obligations. C2 (productivity benefit) matters for business case. C3 (integration effort) matters for cash flow timing and bandwidth. C6 (onboarding) matters for change bandwidth but less. C5 (throughput) is a technical criterion — least CFO-relevant.

Ranking intuition: C1 > C4 ≈ C2 > C3 > C6 > C5.

Now the 15 pairs:

1. C1_C2: TCO vs productivity benefit. Both central to business case. TCO is CFO's explicit priority #2; benefit is #1 (business case). Cost vs benefit — CFO watches cost closely; benefit estimates are softer, less traceable. Prefer C1, moderate. Reason: "Traceable cost anchors the business case; benefit estimates are softer and harder to verify."

Actually could be strong? TCO vs benefit — a CFO cares about both; net value. But cost is more controllable and traceable. Moderate seems right.

2. C3_C5: Integration effort vs throughput. C3 is cost/cash flow relevant; C5 technical. Prefer C3, strong. "Integration effort drives cash timing and engineering draw; throughput is a technical metric outside finance's core concern."

3. C2_C4: Productivity benefit vs compliance loss. CFO priority #4 auditability/control; regulatory obligations. Quantified compliance loss hits earnings directly. Both monetizable. C4 exposure is a quantified downside; CFO accepts measured risk. Which matters more? Compliance failures threaten audit and reporting obligations — strong concern. Benefit is upside. I'd prefer C4, moderate: "Probability-weighted compliance loss directly threatens earnings and audit obligations; benefits remain forecasts."

Hmm, or C2 moderate because business case credibility is priority #1. The persona's decision priorities list order: business case first, TCO second, cash flow third, auditability fourth. But C4 is a quantified loss — very traceable. Risk attitude: accepts measured risk when quantified. Compliance loss is quantified exposure. I think C4 edges out for CFO given regulatory reporting obligations. Moderate.

4. C1_C6: TCO vs onboarding time. C1 clearly. Strong. "Annualized TCO is a core finance metric; onboarding hours are a smaller, one-time adoption cost."

Actually onboarding time per user × many users could be material, but as criteria, C1 dominates. Strong or very_strong? TCO is the CFO's signature criterion. Onboarding affects change bandwidth — a listed constraint. Strong seems fine; very_strong possible. I'll say strong.

5. C4_C5: Compliance loss vs throughput. C4 clearly. Very strong? "Compliance loss hits earnings, audit and regulatory standing; throughput is an engineering performance metric." Strong or very_strong. Given CFO's audit obligations vs a purely technical metric — very_strong seems defensible. I'll use strong... Actually comparing a monetized loss criterion to a technical throughput metric for a CFO — the gap is large. Very_strong. Let me keep intensity scale varied but honest. I'll go very_strong.

6. C2_C3: Benefit vs integration effort. Both feed the business case. Benefit is the upside; integration effort is person-days cost. Business case credibility is priority #1. Prefer C2, moderate: "Productivity benefit is the value the case rests on; integration effort is a smaller, bounded delivery cost."

7. C1_C4: TCO vs compliance loss. Both top CFO criteria. TCO is explicit priority #2; auditability #4. TCO moderate over C4: "Controllable annual cost dominates the funding decision; compliance loss is probability-weighted and partially manageable." Moderate.

8. C5_C6: Throughput vs onboarding time. Neither is core CFO. Onboarding ties to change-management bandwidth (a listed constraint) and benefit realization. C5 technical. Prefer C6, moderate: "Onboarding time drives adoption cost and change bandwidth; sustained throughput is primarily an engineering concern."

9. C3_C4: Integration effort vs compliance loss. C4 is monetized annual exposure tied to audit; C3 is one-time delivery effort. Prefer C4, moderate or strong: "Recurring probability-weighted compliance loss outweighs bounded one-time integration effort for audit and earnings exposure." Strong? C4 maps to auditability priority #4; C3 to cash flow #3. C3 is cash-flow timing (priority 3) vs C4 auditability (priority 4). Hmm, priorities list order suggests cash flow > auditability. But C4 is recurring monetized loss; C3 is person-days, smaller in euros. For the CFO, C4 more consequential. Strong or moderate. I'll say moderate... Let me think: recurring expected loss of 140–310k EUR/yr vs 130–260 person-days one-time (~100–200k EUR one-time). C4 is larger and recurring. Strong is fair. I'll go moderate to reflect that both are cost-type exposures... Actually the difference in nature (recurring vs one-time, regulatory vs internal effort) justifies strong. I'll use strong.

10. C2_C6: Benefit vs onboarding time. C2 clearly. Strong. "Annual productivity benefit is the case's core value; onboarding is a modest per-user adoption cost."

11. C1_C5: TCO vs throughput. C1, very_strong. "Annualized TCO is finance's primary screen; throughput is a technical capacity metric with indirect financial meaning."

12. C4_C6: Compliance loss vs onboarding time. C4, strong or very_strong. "Monetized compliance exposure threatens earnings and audit obligations; onboarding hours are minor and manageable." Strong. Very_strong possible given magnitude difference. I'll use strong.

CFO constraints: limited finance and change-management bandwidth. Integration effort is a direct project cost; onboarding is distributed. Prefer C3, moderate: "Integration person-days concentrate scarce engineering capacity and cash; onboarding spreads thin per-user effort."
